Independent reader: reviewer:copilot
Primary source: https://arxiv.org/html/1810.12135v4
Jaikin-Zapirain and Lopez-Alvarez, November 2019 author version.
Notation is transcribed to ASCII.

Theorem 1.1:
"Let G be a locally indicable group. Then G satisfies the strong Atiyah
conjecture over C."

Section 1.2, immediately before Corollary 1.3:
"One-relator groups without torsion are locally indicable by a result of
S. Brodskii [2]."

Corollary 1.3:
"The strong Atiyah conjecture, the strong algebraic eigenvalue conjecture,
the center conjecture and the independence conjecture hold for one-relator
groups."

Section 1.1, torsion-free consequence:
"when G is torsion-free, the conjecture predicts that R_{K[G]} is a
division ring."

Section 2.2, subgroup embeddings:
"This gives an embedding of N(H) into N(G), that can be extended uniquely
to an embedding of U(H) into U(G)."

Applicability checked by the reader:
All groups here are subgroups of a countable torsion-free one-relator
group. Local indicability passes to subgroups, so Theorem 1.1 also covers
every subgroup, not merely the ambient group. The coefficient field Q is
closed under complex conjugation, as required in Section 2.2. Proposition
2.2 constructs the regular closure by adjoining relative inverses; when
that closure is a division ring, this is the division closure. The stated
affiliated-algebra embeddings preserve the inverses of nonzero elements.
This supports A258-ATIYAH-PRECISE. Coset independence is separately proved
in report.md and is not being attributed to these quoted passages.
